From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - inference observability / hyperscaler comparison - next steps

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the context on your latency targets (p95 < 250ms for inference) and the need for fine-grained cost attribution by product route. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap of what we heard: low-latency user-facing routes (~500 rps peak), internal batch jobs for embeddings, requirement for per-route token/cost breakdown, trace correlation with app traces, and a 6-week POC to validate SLAs and observability.

- How Redwood compares to hyperscalers (short): we typically outperform managed hyperscaler endpoints on unit cost for production workloads thanks to prefix/KV caching and continuous batching, and we provide first-class per-route telemetry out of the box (token-level cost, latency histograms, per-request trace IDs). Hyperscalers offer broad model catalogs but usually require more custom infra/ops to get the same level of observability and rollback automation. I attached a short pull-out that highlights the main diffs.

- Proposed technical tests (what will answer ACME's questions):
  1) Compare p50/p95 latency and per-token cost against AWS Bedrock and OpenAI API for your two representative routes (chat + classification).
  2) Validate trace propagation: correlate Redwood request IDs with your app traces (Datadog/NewRelic).
  3) Show per-route dashboards and a retention policy demo (30d/90d).
  4) Exercise canary rollback and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant.

Next steps:
1) Would you be available for a 60-min technical deep dive next week? Camila (CC'd) will own the SE side.
2) Please share any existing traffic samples (scrubbed) and the two representative prompt templates so we can size the POC.

I've attached our short hyperscaler comparison and an observability proposal.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: observability-proposal.xlsx (POC workbook)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our side: 

- Telemetry: can you confirm whether Redwood exposes per-request trace IDs that can be picked up by Datadog and stitched into our existing service traces? We need end-to-end latency attribution.
- Retention & storage: what's the default retention for request/trace logs and can we configure retention per-route? Any SOC2 concerns around storing request payloads?
- Cost modeling: do you provide exported per-route token and $ cost (CSV or BigQuery) so our FinOps team can run their models?
- POC creds: for the POC, can you provide a short-term tenant or API keys scoped to a staging project, and what's the expected rate limit for a POC (we'll likely push 100-200 rps for a few hours)?

Also, we plan to run parallel tests against Bedrock and OpenAI to compare latency/cost. Are you able to provide suggested test harness scenarios (warm vs cold start, long-context prompts) so we run apples-to-apples?

Happy to do the 60-min deep dive next Tue or Wed afternoon PT.

—Jordan
